Resettlement · Mozambique

Dated structure registers for resettlement cut-off dates

We count and map the structures in your project area on set dates, to size the census, to record what stood there on the cut-off date and to show what has appeared since. For resettlement plans under Mozambique’s regulation and for lenders applying IFC Performance Standard 5. A person reviews every result.

Used in: Oil & gas · Power & utilities · Mining · Project finance & ESIA

Request a proposal See the sample register

What the rules ask for

Mozambique’s resettlement regulation, the sector laws and PS5

Decreto n.º 31/2012

The Regulamento sobre o Processo de Reassentamento Resultante de Actividades Económicas starts with data collection: identifying and delimiting the area, quantifying the affected families, recording its physical characteristics and its ocupação actual, its current occupation (art. 19). It asks for at least four public consultations (art. 23). The plan is part of the environmental impact assessment process, and the district government approves it once the spatial-planning sector has issued its conformity; a technical commission oversees the process.

The sector laws

The rights holder bears resettlement costs after prior consultation, and the people affected must be left with living conditions that are dignified and better than before (Lei n.º 8/2026, art. 61). For power lines, the resettlement and compensation rules apply to the servitude, and no compensation is owed to those who acquired their rights after the line was built (Lei n.º 12/2022, art. 43(8) and (10)).

IFC Performance Standard 5

Lender-funded projects add IFC Performance Standard 5. It asks for a census, in part to discourage ineligible persons, such as opportunistic settlers, from claiming benefits, and, in the absence of host-government procedures, for the client to establish a cut-off date for eligibility (para. 12). The client is not required to compensate or assist those who encroach on the project area after the cut-off date, provided the date has been clearly established and made public (para. 23).

What a dated register supports

A dated, reproducible record of the structures in the project area is useful evidence for both frameworks: it shows what stood where on the date that matters. It supports your census and your IFC Performance Standard 5 cut-off-date records. It does not set the cut-off date, and it does not replace the census, the asset inventory or the consultations.

How it works

Before the census, on the cut-off date, and after

Sizing

Before the census

How many structures stand in the footprint and the buffers around it, where they cluster, and estimated households with the assumptions stated, so the census and asset-inventory teams are sized and routed before they go.

The record

On the cut-off date

A register of the structures on dated imagery, with IDs, coordinates and reviewer categories such as main building, outbuilding, enclosure or under construction, packaged with file fingerprints and an independent timestamp.

Change

After the cut-off date

Re-surveys of the project area and the resettlement villages, with new structures since the cut-off date flagged automatically and confirmed by a reviewer, and a location check for single grievances and claims.

For a route or a line, the same register compares the options first, so the land affected by each option can be weighed; the resettlement process decides what the plan needs. See pipelines and power lines in Mozambique.

The imagery

Why the date on the imagery matters

A cut-off-date record is only as good as the date on its imagery. We build it on imagery with a known capture date: a drone survey, a very-high-resolution satellite scene with its acquisition date, or georeferenced imagery you already hold. Map-service basemaps, which carry no capture date, are never used for it.

Archive coverage and cloud vary by place and season, so the proposal says what exists for your area and dates before you commit. A new satellite capture can be requested when the archive is too old; its date depends on satellite availability and weather, and is never guaranteed.

In Mozambique, a drone baseline needs the Defence authorisation of the survey and the authorisation to release its data to you, and the orthophotos may not be reproduced in the plan, its annexes or anywhere else without authorisation (Lei n.º 6/2024, arts. 13 and 16(1)(c)). Build that into the schedule.

What you receive

  • A structure register: ID, coordinates, category and imagery date
  • Maps of the footprint and buffers
  • A PDF report in Portuguese or English
  • GeoPackage, GeoJSON, KMZ and Shapefile layers
  • An evidence pack with file fingerprints and an independent timestamp
  • Change layers and a notice after each re-survey
  • Estimated households, with the assumptions stated

Who uses it

Resettlement teams, their consultants, and the people who check their work

Resettlement and land teams

At gas, LNG, mining and power projects, planning the census and keeping the cut-off-date record.

ESIA and RAP consultancies

Sizing the census, comparing route options and checking the field inventory, in the formats their teams already use.

Lenders and independent monitors

Checking between site visits what has changed in the project area and the resettlement villages since the cut-off date.

Limits

What a cut-off baseline is not

What it supports

  • Census and asset-inventory planning
  • Your IFC Performance Standard 5 cut-off-date records
  • Community engagement and grievance handling, with dated facts
  • Comparison of route and site options

What it does not do

  • Set the cut-off date or decide who is eligible
  • Carry out the census, the asset inventory or the public consultations
  • Count crops, trees or other improvements: your field teams do that
  • Identify households or people, or see roofs hidden under dense tree cover

Frequently asked questions

Does the imagery set the cut-off date?

No. The cut-off date is set by the host government’s procedures or, where there are none, by the project, and it must be clearly established and made public (IFC Performance Standard 5). Our register records what stood in the project area on a date you choose; it supports the cut-off-date record rather than defining it.

Is the register a substitute for the census or the asset inventory?

No. The census, the inventory of assets and improvements, the public consultations and the eligibility decisions stay with your resettlement team. The register tells the field teams where the structures are, how many to expect and which ones have appeared since the cut-off date.

Can you use drone orthophotos for the baseline?

Yes, where they are flown with the authorisations each survey requires. In Mozambique that includes the Defence authorisation of the survey and the authorisation to release the data, and reproducing orthophotos in the plan or its annexes needs authorisation too (Lei n.º 6/2024, arts. 13 and 16(1)(c)). Dated satellite scenes and imagery you already hold are the alternatives.

Can the register be in Portuguese for the district and the resettlement commission?

Yes. The PDF report is available in Portuguese or English, with maps, the structure register and a photo of each structure, so the same document can go to your team, the district government and the bodies overseeing the process.

Do you identify the households?

No. We map structures, not people. Where you need a planning figure, we estimate households from structure counts with the assumptions stated, for your team to replace with census data.

Setting a cut-off date?

Tell us the footprint, the census window and the date the record must reflect. We reply with the dated imagery that exists for it and a written proposal.
